John Lott. More Guns, Less Crime. Chicago University Press, 1998.

Without even asserting causation, the positive-relationship correlation has a phi value of over 0.90.

Whether the presence of guns results in less crime - and specifically, less violent crime - can be debated all day. That the presence of relatively-high per-capita concentrations of guns accompanies less (violent) crime is, at this point, beyond reproach.

John Lott himself was originally very anti-gun ownership, but after doing the research, faced with reality and sound methodology, reversed his opinion, based on the empirical correlation.

Again, correlation is not and is by no means causation, but the correlation here is almost perfect.

Whether guns result in less crime cannot truly be measured. But that where guns are, less crime tends to happen, this is empirical fact.
